text:
A: Alright? Darren. Can you hear me okay?
B: Hiya! Yes, I can hear you. I'm Blerta, I'm in Newcastle.
A: Newcastle! Long way from me. I'm Bridgwater, Somerset. Where's that to in Newcastle, then?
B: Fenham. It's sort of west of the town centre. Near the Town Moor, if you know it.
A: Never been, mate, I'm ashamed to say. Furthest north I've been is, er, Birmingham, probably. Here, I've got to say, you look just like my daughter's mate in your photo. Kayleigh, she's twenty. Same glasses.
B: Ha, aw. And you look like my dad's taxi mates, sorry. That's a compliment, like, they're all lovely.
A: I'll take that! What do you do, then? I saw the uni hoodie.
B: Yeah, I'm a student. Speech and language therapy, second year. I'm a bit older, though, I'm twenty-seven. I worked in a care home for six years first.
A: Oh, good for you. My wife Donna's a care assistant, residential home. Knackers her out, that job. She comes home and just sits on the settee and doesn't move.
B: It's so hard. Your feet, and your back. My dad's got a bad back from the taxi, so I'm always nagging him about lifting stuff.
A: Don't talk to me about backs. I'm on flooring and tiles at a DIY place in Taunton, lugging boxes of tiles about all day. My knees have had it. I used to play Sunday league till they went.
B: You should do some stretches, honestly. Sorry, I sound like my placement supervisor.
A: Ha, Donna says the same. I just do skittles on a Wednesday. Pint, bit of chat, that's my exercise.
B: Skittles? Nikhil said something about skittles! Was that you?
A: That was me! Spreading the word. Did he tell you about carnival as well?
B: No, what's that?
A: Oh, mate. Bridgwater Carnival. November. Massive carts, all lit up, thousands of bulbs, brass bands, the whole town comes out. I used to build them with my uncle when I was a lad. People come from all over. I go every year without fail, it's the best night of the year in our town, honestly.
B: That sounds amazing. I'd go to that. I'd draw everyone, I keep a sketchbook of people on the Metro.
A: You'd have plenty to draw, mind, half of Somerset's there with a cider. Do you like a drink?
B: I don't drink, actually. I'm Muslim. But I'd come for the lights.
A: Fair enough, there's food, there's chips, you'd be fine. What do you do for tea up there, then? Bit of a Geordie thing?
B: Tea's at six with my mam and dad and my brother. My mam makes Albanian stuff mostly, we're from Kosovo. Flija, it's like layers of pastry, it takes hours.
A: Hours! Ours is meat and two veg. Friday's chippy. I'm not good with anything spicy, mind.
B: Flija's not spicy, you'd be fine! It's just, like, cream and pastry and—
